name: Chaos comes to be
summary: First of all Chaos came to be; then Gaia, Tartarus and Eros. Nothing creates them — they simply emerge.

name: Night and Darkness bear Day
summary: From Chaos come Erebus and Night; Night, joined with Erebus, bears the bright Aether and Day.

name: Earth bears Sky and Sea
summary: Gaia bears starry Uranus, equal to herself, to cover her on every side, and the barren sea Pontus — both without a partner.

name: Birth of the Titans, Cyclopes and Hundred-Handers
summary: Gaia and Uranus produce twelve Titans, youngest Cronus; then the three Cyclopes and the three Hundred-Handers. Uranus hates them and pushes them back into the earth.

name: Cronus overthrows Uranus
summary: Gaia forges a sickle of adamant. Cronus ambushes his father as he lies over the earth and castrates him, taking the rule of the world.

name: Aphrodite rises from the foam (Hesiod's account)
summary: The severed genitals fall into the sea; from the white foam around them a goddess grows and comes ashore at Cyprus. Homer gives a different parentage (Zeus and Dione), so this event belongs to Hesiod's version only.

name: Cronus swallows his children
summary: Warned that a son will overthrow him, Cronus swallows each child as soon as Rhea gives birth.

name: Zeus is hidden on Crete
summary: Rhea gives birth to Zeus in secret on Crete and hands Cronus a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes, which he swallows.

name: Cronus disgorges his children
summary: Cronus is made to vomit up the stone and then his children. Zeus frees the Cyclopes, who give him thunder and lightning.

name: The War of the Titans
summary: For ten years the Olympians fight from Olympus against the Titans on Othrys. Zeus releases the Hundred-Handers, unleashes his thunderbolts, and the earth and sea boil.

name: Titans bound in Tartarus
summary: The defeated Titans are chained in Tartarus behind bronze gates, guarded by the Hundred-Handers. Atlas is set to hold up the sky.

name: Zeus defeats Typhon
summary: Gaia and Tartarus bring forth Typhon, a monster of a hundred snake heads. Zeus scorches him with lightning and hurls him into Tartarus.

name: The world divided by lot
summary: The three sons of Cronus draw lots: Zeus wins the sky, Poseidon the sea, Hades the gloom below. Earth and Olympus remain common to all.

name: Athena born from Zeus' head
summary: Zeus swallows the pregnant Metis to stop her bearing a son who would rule. Athena later springs from his head, fully armed.

name: Leto gives birth on Delos
summary: Refused by every land, Leto is welcomed by the little island of Delos, where she bears Apollo (and, in the tradition, Artemis).

name: Apollo founds his oracle at Pytho
summary: Apollo kills the she-dragon at Pytho, below Parnassus, and establishes his oracle there, bringing Cretan sailors to be his priests.

name: Hermes steals Apollo's cattle
summary: Born at dawn in Maia's cave, Hermes invents the lyre by midday and steals Apollo's cattle by evening. Zeus makes them reconcile.

name: Prometheus steals fire
summary: At Mecone, Prometheus tricks Zeus over the sacrificial portions. Zeus withholds fire; Prometheus steals it in a fennel stalk, and is chained and tormented by an eagle.

name: The abduction of Persephone
summary: Hades seizes Persephone in his chariot. Demeter searches, then halts all growth until Zeus sends Hermes to bring her back — but she has eaten a pomegranate seed and must return below for part of each year.

name: Dionysus, twice born
summary: Semele is destroyed by Zeus' true form; Zeus rescues the unborn child and carries him in his thigh until his second birth.

name: Zeus makes the race of heroes
summary: Hesiod's fourth race of humankind: the godlike heroes, called demigods, who fought at Thebes and Troy. Some die; others are sent to the Isles of the Blessed.

name: The labours of Heracles
summary: Bound to serve Eurystheus, Heracles kills the Nemean lion and the Hydra, fetches the apples of the Hesperides with Atlas' help, drags Cerberus from the underworld, and frees Prometheus.

name: The voyage of the Argo
summary: Jason gathers the Argonauts and sails to Colchis for the Golden Fleece, which he wins with Medea's help.

name: Wedding of Peleus and Thetis
summary: The gods attend the wedding. Strife, uninvited, throws a golden apple 'for the fairest', and Hera, Athena and Aphrodite each claim it.

name: The Judgement of Paris
summary: Hermes leads the three goddesses to Paris on Mount Ida. He awards the apple to Aphrodite, who promises him Helen, wife of Menelaus.

name: The Trojan War (as narrative)
summary: The Greeks besiege Troy for ten years. In the tenth, Achilles quarrels with Agamemnon, withdraws, returns to kill Hector, and gives the body back to Priam. This is the myth; whether any historical war lies behind it is a separate, historical question.

name: The wooden horse and the sack of Troy
summary: Odysseus devises the wooden horse; Greeks hidden inside open the gates, and Troy is sacked. Told by Demodocus in the Odyssey and at length in later poems.

name: Agamemnon's homecoming
summary: Agamemnon reaches Mycenae and is killed at a feast by Aegisthus and Clytemnestra — the Odyssey's dark mirror of Odysseus' return.

name: The return of Odysseus
summary: Ten years of wandering: the Cicones, Lotus-Eaters, Cyclops, Aeolus, Laestrygonians, Circe, the underworld, Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis, the cattle of the Sun, Calypso, the Phaeacians — and finally Ithaca.
